commands.name: conductor
commands.description: Workflow designer and run view: no argument opens the board (a run in progress, the project last opened, or the start screen to pick one); with a description, Claude drafts a new project for it; min and max move the designer between its pane and the band above the prompt
commands.argumentHint: [what the workflow should do | min | max]
commands.output: Open a saved project in the pane, or start a new one from a template.

tools.name: project
tools.description:
Reads and edits the user's Conductor workflow project: the board of blocks they see, saved at .claude/workflow-conductor/<name>.json. Use it whenever the user asks to draft, add, change, move or remove workflow blocks or steps ("add a verify after n3", "this block"); do not edit that file by hand. A project is a spec the user reviews, not a script: never run it from here.
Actions: read = the project JSON, the block selected on the board ("this block") and the lints. Read before you describe, review or edit a project, unless a Conductor note with the prompt has told you what changed: the user changes the board by hand between your turns, so what you read or wrote earlier may be gone (every answer names the revision it shows). apply = `ops` in order, all or nothing. write = replace the whole tree with `nodes` (drafting, large restructures). attach = a write, with `match`, of a project OF the workflow run tracked now: the run shows on it. An edit shows on the board at once and returns the lints: fix them or tell the user.
Block: { id, type, kind?, name, logic?, knobs?, match?, children? }. Ids (n1, n2…) are assigned for you and never change. name is a short label; logic is free text saying what the block should do. Order is execution order. Only containers hold children. Blocks directly inside a branch are its arms (one runs, picked by its `condition`), and directly inside a parallel they run side by side: to run two blocks one after the other there, put both in a pipeline. Every project starts with its start block: it is not added, moved or removed, and it alone has the knobs `goal` (the goal of the whole workflow, in a sentence: set it when drafting, keep it true) and `args` (the workflow's input, or unset for none). Update it by id; in a write, put it first, or leave it out to keep it as it is.
Types:
- agent: Performs a task. Use when a step needs reading or judgment: search, review, write, decide.
- pipeline (container): Per-item chain of steps. Use when each item takes several steps and no step needs all items at once.
- parallel (container): Concurrent; awaits all. Use when the next step needs every result together: merge, compare, pick.
- loop (container): Repeat until stop rule. Use when you cannot tell up front how many rounds it takes; say when it stops.
- branch (container): If/else on a result. Use when a result decides what runs next, e.g. nothing found: skip the checks.
- subworkflow: Run a saved workflow. Use when a saved workflow already does this part.
- code: Plain JS, no tokens. Use when the step is exact and mechanical: never spend an agent on it.
- start: Entry: goal and args. Use when always: every project has one, first.
Kinds: `kind` names the pattern a block is used for (each explained on `kind` in the schema); leave it out for the plain block. agent: scout, check, verify, judge, critic, merge, classify. loop: count, pass, dry, converged, target, budget. parallel: each, sweep, attempts. branch: guard, route.
Knobs, all optional, explained on `knobs` in the schema: goal, args, prompt, output, model, effort, isolation, agentType, oncePer, stopCondition, condition.
